item.text: I’m checking the 2024 macro record from multiple angles first: growth path, fiscal stance, policy credibility, and whether the government corrected course under pressure. After that I’ll synthesize only claim-level evidence for 5B.10.

item.text:
**Assessment**
Mixed to slightly negative. Thailand under Srettha looked more stable than crisis-ridden, but the evidence does not show a clearly stronger economic trajectory by the time he left office. Growth improved only modestly, inflation stayed low, and investment signals were decent, but the flagship stimulus strategy raised fiscal-risk concerns and policy credibility weakened under political pressure.

**Evidence**
- **Thailand Systematic Country Diagnostic Update 2024: Shifting Gears - Toward Sustainable Growth and Inclusive Prosperity** | World Bank | 2024 | [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/thailand/publication/thailand-scd2024) | The Bank says Thailand had preserved macroeconomic and financial stability, but recovery still lagged ASEAN peers because of exposure to weak global tourism and trade. This is the clearest external-constraint context: Srettha inherited a slow recovery, not a strong rebound. `5B.10`, `5B.9`
- **Thailand Economic Monitor July 2024: Unlocking the Growth Potential of Secondary Cities** | World Bank | July 3, 2024 | [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/thailand/publication/temjuly2024) | The Bank projected 2.4% growth in 2024, up from 1.9% in 2023, with inflation at 0.7%, but also warned that public debt and the fiscal deficit would rise as stimulus measures were implemented. That supports a modest-improvement reading, but not a durable stronger trajectory. `5B.10`, `5B.6`, `5B.9`
- **Monetary Policy Committee’s Decision 3/2024** | Bank of Thailand | June 12, 2024 | [URL](https://www.bot.or.th/en/news-and-media/news/news-20240612.html) | The BOT said the economy was still expanding on domestic demand and tourism, but exports remained subdued and structural challenges persisted; it also favored targeted SME credit support. This is positive on stabilization, but it is still a slow, constrained recovery. `5B.10`, `5B.9`
- **Thailand sees at least $22 billion investment pledges in 2024** | Reuters via Investing.com | June 14, 2024 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/thailand-sees-at-least-22-billion-investment-pledges-in-2024-3484417) | Reuters reported strong first-quarter investment applications and a large pipeline of pledged investment in productive sectors. This is one of the best positive signals that the administration was not merely consuming capital but still attracting productive investment. `5B.10`, `5B.6`
- **Thailand's cabinet approves $13.5 billion digital wallet handout** | Reuters via Investing.com | April 23, 2024 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/thailands-cabinet-approves-135-billion-digital-wallet-handout-3390007) | The government approved a broad 10,000-baht transfer to 50 million people, and Reuters noted immediate debt and fiscal-risk criticism. That points to popularity-driven macro management rather than a clearly stronger long-run trajectory. `5B.10`, `5B.7`, `5B.8`, `5B.9`
- **Thai central bank holds key rate, defies government calls for cuts** | Reuters via Investing.com | April 10, 2024 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/thai-central-bank-holds-key-rate-defies-government-calls-for-cuts-3372713) | Reuters reported repeated government pressure for rate cuts, while the BOT held rates to protect macro-financial stability. This weakens the case that Srettha handled macro constraints with discipline or deference to technocratic judgment. `5B.10`, `5B.7`, `5B.9`
- **Analysis-Political turmoil threatens prospects of Thailand's floundering economy** | Reuters via Investing.com | August 15, 2024 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/analysispolitical-turmoil-threatens-prospects-of-thailands-floundering-economy-3573010) | Reuters described 1.5% Q1 growth, household debt at 90.8% of GDP, weak industrial and consumer sentiment, and uncertainty over the budget and handout scheme after Srettha’s dismissal. This is strong negative evidence that the economy was still fragile and politically exposed when he left. `5B.10`, `5B.9`
- **Thailand's $13 billion digital handout scheme to include cash payments, PM says** | Reuters via Investing.com | September 3, 2024 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/thai-pm-says-part-of-13-billion-digital-wallet-stimulus-to-be-in-cash-3597164) | The later shift from a pure digital-wallet design to partial cash payments shows some correction, but it reads more like tactical compromise than a decisive, evidence-led course correction. `5B.10`, `5B.9`

**Gap**
- I did not find direct evidence of a large, completed structural reform package under Srettha that clearly outperformed inherited conditions.
- The strongest positive evidence is modest: low inflation, some investment momentum, and preservation of macro stability.
- Because Srettha was removed on August 14, 2024, there is no clean year-end outcome attributable solely to him.
